newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly lower, volume light.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly lower, volume light.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly lower Monday, but not before gold made a new two-month high and silver a new four-month high.

"The gold rally may have a way to go, as funds have only reduced their net short position by half in recent weeks and, as Friday's jump demonstrated, the market can get illiquid when the upside is tested," Friedberg Mercantile Group fund manager, Chris Foster said.
"But our official view is that we remain sceptical of the rally unless there is a serious breakdown in financial markets," he said.
COMEX April gold ended down $1.30 an ounce at $364.00, after seeing a 366.00-363.50 range, with estimated total volume for the gold strip at 25,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold closed quoted $361.70/20, compared with the London Monday afternoon fix at $362.15, and the New York close Friday around $363.50/00.

The recovery in gold from three year lows in February was driven by fund shortcovering, with "large trader" net short positions falling to 21,241 contracts on February 25, from 46,650 lots two weeks earlier, according to the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report issued Friday.
But open interest in COMEX gold jumped 4,783 lots Friday, after declining by more than 23,000 contracts in the previous two weeks.

Resistance is now seen around $370 in both spot gold and COMEX April gold, the level from which gold broke down in late 1996, before extending its year-long decline to three year lows around $336, analysts said.
"We seen the very top end of the range as being $365-370 basis spot and the bottom end $345-350," Merrill Lynch analyst Ted Arnold said in a report.
"This doesn't mean that the bear market is over, only that this is a temporary pause in what is probably a downward sloping price trend over coming years," he said.
"The bull news for gold is that physical demand proved to be very strong in India, and parts of Asia and the Middle East when prices hit a three-and-a-half year low in January."
"So on that evidence one would assume that $335-340 is a reasonably good support level for physical demand."
COMEX gold's nearby-active-month 20-day historical volatility has risen to around 12 percent in the past two months, after declining to around four percent in late 1996.
Gold has also recovered faster than silver in the past two weeks, after silver staged its own recovery starting in January, leaving funds net long silver, analysts said.
"Large traders" were net long 26,348 lots in COMEX silver futures as of February 25, up from 7,241 lots two weeks earlier, according to the CFTC data.
COMEX May silver ended down 2.0 cents at $5.345 Monday though, after trading in a $5.435-5.310 range, on total estimated volume for the silver strip of 22,000 lots.
In the platinum group of metals, NYMEX April platinum ended down $4.60 an ounce at $391.50, after failing to hold above $400 an ounce Friday.
But ongoing concerns about Russian supplies saw NYMEX June palladium end up $1.25 at $156.25.
Monday was first notice day for March platinum and palladium, but there is no open interest in March platinum and only 1,829 remaining March palladium.
In news Monday, workers at Russia's Norilsk plant gave management a 10-day deadline to meet wage arrears demand but management said it could not meet the deadline.
Workers have threatened to strike from March 15.
Russia is the world's main supplier of palladium and the second largest supplier of platinum, while Japan is the world's largest consumer of both metals.
--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641
